title: The soil pile, as depth over time — the card I should have sent
question: Watch the ground line rise in the first clip and hold flat in the second. Is that the floor you wanted — or is it still filling too fast?
context_md:
My last card asked you to compare three stills of a stand and you said, fairly, *"What am i supposed to be looking at."* That was the card failing, not the change. You complained about **a giant pile of soil** — a depth that builds up — and I sent you a grid of single moments framed on the canopy. Depth over time is not something a still can show.

So this is the same question re-asked properly: **cropped to the floor with the sky cut away, and animated over 12,000 frames** so the accumulation is the thing moving.

I also had to build the measurement your words named, because nothing in the engine counted it — soil cells in the world, sampled every 600 frames.

| frame | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 600 | 3,470 | 3,429 |
| 3,000 | 3,333 | 3,169 |
| 6,000 | 3,815 | 2,973 |
| 9,000 | 5,235 | 3,091 |
| 12,000 | **6,971** | **3,358** |

The floor **doubles** in the before clip and **ends where it started** in the after.

**Two things I want you to distrust me on:**

1. *Both* clips dip before frame 6,000 — soil leaves as well as arrives, and I do not yet know what consumes it. So the after clip is not "decay stopped", it is "decay stopped outrunning whatever removes it".
2. The after world carries **more leaf on the plants** (33,425 living cells against 28,776) — the leaves that stop falling stay up there. If the crowns now read as one mass instead of separate stands, that is the cost of this, and I would rather hear it now. I am sending a separate card framed on the crowns for exactly that.

What changed: the quarter leaf-fall rate you already picked ("C is best") now applies to all four woody species the world sows, not just `tree`. It was only on `tree` because the other three arrived in a later merge.
